name: Can I be fired for refusing to do something illegal?
description: No, generally you cannot be legally fired for refusing an illegal act, as this is considered wrongful termination under public policy.

mainEntity.name: Can I be fired for refusing to do something illegal?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you generally cannot be legally fired for refusing to perform an illegal act, such as falsifying records, engaging in fraud, or violating safety regulations. This is considered a form of wrongful termination under public policy exceptions to at-will employment. If you are terminated for refusing to participate in illegal activity, you may have grounds for a wrongful termination claim.
